community: Indigenous reserves (unnamed; in ridings around Lethbridge)

submitter_note: Danielle Larivee, former MLA Lesser Slave Lake, resident of Slave Lake
community: Woodland Cree First Nation; Kee Tas Kee Now Tribal Council nations; Treaty 8 nations; Métis settlements in Lesser Slave Lake
request: keep Woodland Cree with the other Kee Tas Kee Now Tribal Council nations in Lesser Slave Lake rather than moving it to Peace River, and generally keep tribal council nations, treaty organizations and Métis settlements together, adding Indigenous communities to Lesser Slave Lake rather than non-Indigenous ones
quote: I think it’s really important that all the members of the Kee Tas Kee Now Tribal Council continue to be together
note: Answering Commissioner Clark's question about the Peace River mayor's idea of moving Woodland Cree to Peace River: she opposes 'hive them off'. Earlier (EB-416) general request: 'We need to make sure that the nations for sure for each tribal council are connected together, that each treaty organization is ideally clustered together as much as possible, and keep as many Métis settlements together as possible'. Also suggests including additional settlements or Indigenous communities in Lesser Slave Lake to gain population. Page: quote follows the [EB-416] marker with no later marker in the record; footer convention gives EB-417. She does not say she is a member of a nation.
